I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the system I know best, it fits the climate, and it spreads my work across the year. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage that crop through spring and harvest it in early summer. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize on the same land. At my age, I want a cropping pattern that is steady, familiar, easy to manage with machines, and less risky than trying specialty crops. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I care most about stable emergence, uniform growth, and dependable yield. I will use moderate fertilizer rather than chasing the very highest yield, because that keeps costs and lodging risk under control. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my conditions and machinery. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because spring here is often dry, while maize usually benefits more from rainfall but still needs some water at key stages. I will spray only as much as needed to keep common diseases, weeds, and insects under control without making the season too expensive.
